A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Deep Feature Deformation Weights. All 17 pages of each version, including the supplementary material, are readable and support comparison of text, equations, tables, and figures.

before.justification: V1 reports original deformation experiments, timing comparisons, ablations, robustness examples, and a user study.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds dense-handle examples, surface-distortion measurements, and a second user study.

M1.justification: The feature field, distillation objective, feature-proximity weights, constraints, locality weighting, and symmetry procedure remain substantively unchanged. V2 Equation (1) incorporates the simulated-control-point formulation already documented in v1 Appendix I, Equation (10); its relocation does not establish a new method.

E1.justification: Both versions cover handle-based deformation using APAP-Bench 3D, DMH/ShapeNet cars, tables and chairs, Objaverse objects, and Stanford scanned meshes. The added analyses change control configurations and evaluation criteria within these deformation domains, without establishing distinct dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: The existing comparisons retain ARAP, biharmonic/DMH, APAP, NeuralMLS, and the OptCtrlPoints rebinding comparison. The new realism study uses existing baselines. Figure 22 compares against ARAP; Implicit-ARAP is cited as the source of metrics, not evaluated as a new comparator.

E3.justification: The reported distillation settings change from 100 views and 10 iterations to 24 views and 15 iterations, without establishing which experiments were rerun. V2 also adds dense-handle testing, four surface-distortion metrics, and a 23-participant realism study covering 14 deformation cases. The first study's main-text count changes from 32 to 37, matching v1's table and appendix rather than demonstrating increased recruitment.

E4.justification: New Appendix G/Figure 21 checks DFD using the dense handle configurations previously used by baselines. Appendix H/Figure 22 adds two cases examining geometric distortion versus perceived deformation quality. These are targeted supplementary analyses; the existing encoder, distillation, topology, resolution, and generalization analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version adds seed reporting, uncertainty intervals, or formal significance testing relative to the other. Table 3 retains the same 1,000 random handle-set samples. Participant counts and the additional study concern evaluation sample sizes, not new uncertainty-estimation practices.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantial new empirical findings: the realism study reports DFD selected 64% of the time versus ARAP's 17.7%, and Figure 22 reports greater geometric distortion for DFD in two cases, including bench area change of 40.6% versus ARAP's 13.8%. Dense-handle outputs are also added. Existing Tables 2–3 and timing graphics remain unchanged; the new realism percentages are not directly comparable with the earlier desirability percentages.

T1.justification: V1 Appendix I claims its extension trivially satisfies partition of unity/affine precision. V2 explicitly restricts the partition-of-unity guarantee to configurations whose handle weights sum to at most one and acknowledges its absence for dense configurations. This corrects the stated mathematical guarantee while retaining the underlying formula.

C1.justification: The central contributions remain feature-based deformation weights, barycentric distillation, interactive control, and symmetry detection. The abstract/introduction relax preprocessing claims from under a minute to minutes or a few minutes, and Table 1 replaces size invariance with size robustness.

C2.justification: V2 distinguishes visual symmetry from intrinsic and extrinsic geometric symmetry, qualifies partition-of-unity applicability, and explains why lower geometric distortion need not imply more realistic deformation. It also adds interpretation of baseline sensitivity to handle placement. Existing limitations concerning per-shape optimization and extreme-deformation collapse remain.

D1.justification: Technical Details revises the view and iteration counts, while retaining the four-layer MLP, normalization, 512-by-512 rendering, decimation implementation, and A40 hardware information. The abstract adds a project-page address. These are limited changes to reproducibility and access documentation.

R1.justification: V2 adds Implicit-ARAP, iWires, Global Intrinsic Symmetries of Shapes, and 3DN, while removing the PRIMO and adaptive rigid-cell deformation references. Related work more explicitly positions DFD around structure-preserving, potentially surface-distorting edits, refining the existing positioning rather than replacing it.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related-work discussion, mathematical exposition, and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting, alongside widespread changes from semantic terminology to visual or structural terminology. Appendix sections are reorganized and acknowledgements added. Some table references regress into incorrect or unhelpful section references.

P2.justification: V2 adds Figures 21, 22, and 24; v1's user-study Figure 21 becomes Figure 23. Several existing figures move, table captions switch below the tables, and appendix layouts are rearranged. Most existing visual results and timing graphics are retained, with some image-resolution changes.

improvement.justification: V2 improves precision by qualifying partition of unity, reconciling the first study's participant count, and moderating speed claims. Dense-handle checks, distortion measurements, and the separate realism study provide useful additional evidence. The overall gain is limited: most results remain unchanged, the revised training settings are not clearly connected to rerun results, and several cross-references become less accurate.
